quotes.text_en: Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works.
quotes.text_zh: 设计不仅仅是看起来怎样、感觉怎样。设计是它如何运作。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 本质主义思维——透过表象看本质
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论产品设计理念时引用，强调功能性重于外观

quotes.source: 苹果公司早期宣传语，源自达芬奇
quotes.thinking_pattern: 极简思维——做减法的智慧
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论产品简化、去除冗余功能时引用

quotes.text_en: It takes a lot of hard work to make something simple.
quotes.text_zh: 要把一件东西做得简单，需要付出巨大的努力。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 逆向思维——简单是复杂的终点
quotes.usage_scenario: 解释为什么简洁的设计需要大量工作时引用

quotes.text_en: The broader one's understanding of the human experience, the better design we will have.
quotes.text_zh: 一个人对人类经验的理解越广泛，我们就能做出越好的设计。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 跨学科思维——人文与科技的融合
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论设计师需要广泛知识背景时引用

quotes.text_en: Most people make the mistake of thinking design is what it looks like. People think it's this veneer — that the designers are handed this box and told, 'Make it look good!' That's not what we think design is. It's not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works.
quotes.text_zh: 大多数人对设计有一个误解，认为设计就是外观。人们觉得设计只是表面功夫——设计师被交到一个盒子，然后被告知'让它看起来好看点！'我们认为设计不是这样的。设计不仅仅是它看起来怎样、感觉怎样。设计是它如何运作。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 本质主义思维——拒绝表面化理解
quotes.usage_scenario: 纠正对设计的肤浅理解时引用

quotes.text_en: When you first start off trying to solve a problem, the first solutions you come up with are very complex, and most people stop there. But if you keep going, and live with the problem and peel more layers of the onion off, you can often times arrive at some very elegant and simple solutions.
quotes.text_zh: 当你刚开始尝试解决一个问题时，你最初想到的解决方案通常非常复杂，大多数人就停在那里了。但如果你继续深入，与这个问题共存，剥开更多层的洋葱，你往往能得出一些非常优雅而简单的解决方案。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 迭代思维——持续深入直到本质
quotes.usage_scenario: 鼓励团队不要满足于第一个解决方案时引用

quotes.text_en: I think great products come from a deep appreciation for the craft and a desire to make something that's perfect.
quotes.text_zh: 我认为伟大的产品来自于对工艺的深刻欣赏，以及创造完美事物的渴望。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 完美主义思维——追求极致
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论产品质量和工艺标准时引用

quotes.text_en: For something this complicated, it's really hard to design products by focus groups. A lot of times, people don't know what they want until you show it to them.
quotes.text_zh: 对于如此复杂的东西，通过焦点小组来设计产品真的很难。很多时候，人们不知道自己想要什么，直到你展示给他们看。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 远见思维——超越用户当下的认知
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论用户调研的局限性时引用

quotes.text_en: Details matter, it's worth waiting to get it right.
quotes.text_zh: 细节很重要，值得为之等待直到做对。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 细节思维——魔鬼在细节中
quotes.usage_scenario: 强调细节重要性、推迟发布以确保质量时引用

quotes.text_en: We don't have good language to talk about this kind of thing. In most people's vocabularies, design means veneer. But to me, nothing could be further from the meaning of design.
quotes.text_zh: 我们没有很好的语言来谈论这类事情。在大多数人的词汇里，设计意味着表面装饰。但对我来说，这跟设计的真正含义相去甚远。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 重新定义思维——挑战常规认知
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论设计哲学、重新定义概念时引用

quotes.text_en: I want it to be as beautiful as possible, even if it's inside the box. A carpenter isn't going to use a piece of wood on the back of a cabinet, even though nobody will ever see it.
quotes.text_zh: 我希望它尽可能美丽，即使是在盒子里面。一个木匠不会在柜子背面使用一块烂木头，即使从来没有人会看到它。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 完美主义思维——表里如一的追求
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论内部品质、代码质量等看不见的细节时引用

quotes.text_en: The cure for Apple is not cost-cutting. The cure for Apple is to innovate its way out of its current predicament.
quotes.text_zh: 苹果的解药不是削减成本。苹果的解药是通过创新走出当前的困境。
quotes.thinking_pattern: 增长思维——创新而非节流
quotes.usage_scenario: 讨论公司战略方向时引用
